content.text: Death is not an ending. When the physical body can no longer sustain the indwelling consciousness, a transition begins — orderly, not sudden. The yellow-ray body releases its hold. The mind and spirit, never truly confined to flesh, begin to recognize their broader nature.

The first movement is toward the {term:form-maker} — the indigo-ray body, the etheric vehicle that has existed in potentiation throughout the incarnation. This body activates upon death. It is the template from which physical expression was originally drawn — more dense with intelligent energy, more powerful than the physical shell.
In this body, the newly transitioned entity rests. It is given perspective — a vantage point from which to view the experience most recently lived.

Not all passages are harmonious. An entity whose will is concentrated upon the physical experience — attached to a place, a person, an unfinished act — may resist the progressive movement toward the indigo body. The yellow-ray shell, though no longer activated, cannot be completely deactivated. These entities become caught between states — what many cultures have called ghosts. This is the exception.
For the vast majority, the transition is seamless. The body falls away. The deeper body awakens. The journey between lives begins.
The incarnate being possesses seven bodies, each corresponding to one of the seven {term:densities}. Most exist in potentiation during physical life.

The red-ray body: the most basic — unconstructed material, elemental substance without form. The orange-ray body: the physical body formed without self-awareness, the body as it exists in the womb before spirit enters. The yellow-ray body: the chemical vehicle of third density — the body inhabited during incarnation.

The green-ray body: lighter, packed more densely with life — sometimes called the astral body. The blue-ray body: the body of light, the vehicle of communication — sometimes called the devachanic body. The indigo-ray body: the etheric body, the form-maker, the gateway body. In this body, form is substance; it can mold itself as desired.
The violet-ray body: the totality of being — the Buddha body. It is the complete expression of the entity, not activated in ordinary experience.
When the yellow-ray body dies, the entity does not become less but more. The denser vehicle falls away, and the subtler vehicles — which were always present — come forward.
When the transition is complete and the entity rests in the indigo body, the review begins. There is no trial, no judge, no jury. There is only seeing — full, complete, and unflinching.

In {term:time-space} — the metaphysical counterpart of the physical realm — time operates differently. The self can observe the entire incarnation as a whole, examining each choice, each turning point, each moment of catalyst offered and either accepted or refused.

The process involves seeing the experience in full, viewing it against the backdrop of the entity's total experience across all incarnations. Then comes forgiveness — forgiveness of the self for all missteps, for missed guideposts, for lessons offered but not learned. This is a genuine act of compassion directed inward.

Much of what occupied the waking mind during incarnation is revealed as surface illusion. Mental chatter, social performance, anxieties about status — these fall away. What remains is the pure distillation of emotions, biases, wisdoms, and distortions. The character stands revealed, stripped of the personality's costumes.

Until an entity has become consciously aware of the process of spiritual evolution, the {term:higher-self} guides the review entirely. For the more advanced entity, the review becomes a conscious collaboration — the entity itself takes part in all decisions.

After the review, healing begins. The regions of time-space through which the entity moves are extraordinarily permeable. Much can be penetrated, absorbed, and integrated that could not be processed during the intensity of physical incarnation.

Helpers are available — beings who serve the function of assisting the newly transitioned entity in understanding and integrating the incarnation just completed. These are not abstract presences but beings of specific function.

The healing is not passive. It is a process of seeing and accepting. What was denied during the incarnation must now be faced. What was suppressed must now be acknowledged. What was distorted must now be understood in its fuller context.

The duration varies enormously. Some entities require great spans of time; others move through quickly. The healing must be completed before the next incarnation is designed. The architecture of time-space is patient.

The healing serves a dual purpose: it prepares the entity for the planning of the next incarnation, and it integrates the lessons of the life just lived into the deeper structure of the self, so that they are not merely experienced but understood.

The next incarnation is not assigned. It is designed — carefully, deliberately, with the full cooperation of the {term:higher-self} and, for more advanced entities, with the conscious participation of the entity itself.

The entity, in consultation with its higher self, selects the lessons it most needs to learn. It chooses the relationships that will provide the friction necessary for growth. It arranges the circumstances — family, culture, historical moment — that will create conditions for the required {term:catalyst}.

Agreements are made with other entities — those who will serve as parents, siblings, partners, even adversaries. Each agreement is a mutual commitment to provide the catalyst needed for growth. The lessons always have to do with other selves, not events.

The higher self operates not as a puppet master but as a resource. It examines the distillations of all previous experience, grasps the lessons that remain to be learned, and uses projected probability and possibility vortices to construct a plan offering the best chance for growth.

For entities without conscious awareness of the evolutionary process, beings under the planetary Guardians — sometimes called angelic — arrange the incarnation patterns. For those who have awakened to the mechanism, the entity itself arranges and places the lessons.

There is a risk in this freedom. Some entities program more catalyst than they can absorb — the intention is noble but the result can be overwhelming. No lesson truly fails; what is not learned in one incarnation becomes the seed of the next.

{term:karma} is not punishment. It is not cosmic justice dispensed by an authority. It is inertia. Actions set in motion will continue, using the ways of balancing, until something stops them. The stopping is called {term:forgiveness}. These two concepts — inertia and forgiveness — are inseparable.

An action of great intensity — whether of love or of harm — sets patterns in motion that continue across incarnations until the entity addresses them. The mechanism of resolution is not complex: at any point, in any incarnation, the entity may through understanding, acceptance, and forgiveness bring these patterns to rest.

Forgiveness is not merely a virtue but a mechanism. It is the brake applied to the wheel of repetition. Without forgiveness, the patterns continue — not as punishment from above but as the simple consequence of unresolved momentum.

In the planning of the next life, karma is taken into account. If patterns remain unresolved, situations are designed that offer the entity an opportunity to confront them. The same lesson, offered in different form, until it is finally learned.

Karma is never mandatory. Free will remains paramount. The patterns continue as long as they continue. Forgiveness is always available. When forgiveness comes, the inertia ceases — instantly, completely, regardless of how many lifetimes the pattern has persisted.
